description: Shared-dependency layer for the AGENT estate — the common-cause nodes every workflow rides on. The structural twin of rac's data/dependency_catalog.json: same mechanism (one structural event UNDER many risks at once), different substrate (the agent layer instead of the infrastructure layer).
units_note: STRUCTURAL LAYER, NOT A LOSS MODEL: atg's currency is workflows, traced actions and findings — there is deliberately NO frequency×severity dollar model here (the rac spoke prices the infrastructure analogs; production would attach fitted agent-incident history before pricing this layer). Blast radii are DERIVED at build time from the same traces and lineage the dashboard renders — the catalog declares WHAT each node underlies (lineage node or action types), never the counts.
provenance_note: OPERATOR_CALIBRATED structure anchored to named public incidents. Where the class has no public incident of record at this archetype (a first-party agent orchestrator), anchors are labeled CLASS_ANALOG and borrow the nearest control-plane precedent — declared, not hidden.

nodes.name: Agent orchestrator (routing & delegation plane)

loss.effect: Every workflow stalls — no delegation, no tool calls, no decisions. The estate's single structural hub: its loss IS the estate's loss.

blindness.effect: Routing continues but trace emission breaks — actions still happen, UNGOVERNED. A lineage break at estate scale: every downstream evidence trail is severed while work continues, and multi-agent loops run uncounted.

anchors.name: Meta control-plane loss
anchors.label: CLASS_ANALOG
anchors.summary: The control plane that routes everything goes down and takes the tools that would fix it — no public agent-orchestrator incident of record at this archetype; this is the nearest control-plane precedent, declared as an analog.

anchors.name: Reddit Pi-Day K8s control-plane outage
anchors.label: CLASS_ANALOG
anchors.summary: A control-plane upgrade takes the whole estate down for hours — the orchestrator is the agent estate's etcd.

nodes.mitigation_note: The one node whose blast radius the lineage graph itself proves: it transits every workflow. Isolation options are structural (per-domain orchestrators, static fallback routing), not control tweaks.

nodes.name: Model provider (hosted LLM inference)

loss.effect: Every agent that reasons stops reasoning — inference is the substrate the estate runs on, and a provider outage is a same-hour, all-workflows event.

blindness.effect: The provider degrades SILENTLY — a model swap, a quality regression, a routing change. Agents keep producing output that clears no bar: low-confidence decisions ship and PII discipline slips, with nothing down to alarm on.

anchors.name: OpenAI major API outage
anchors.summary: API and ChatGPT down for hours (DDoS-attributed) — every dependent product's agent layer stalled at once; the pure form of this node's loss mode.

anchors.name: ChatGPT/API multi-hour degradation
anchors.summary: Elevated errors across the API during peak hours — dependent workflows degraded together, not independently.

nodes.mitigation_note: Multi-provider failover is the region-failover of the agent estate — and carries the same failover-failure risk class rac prices on cloud_region (the fallback model behaves differently under the same prompts).

nodes.name: Tool / MCP registry (agent supply chain)

loss.effect: Tool resolution fails — every workflow that executes a tool or calls an external API stalls at the call site.

blindness.effect: The registry is POISONED rather than down — a malicious or tampered tool description executes with the agent's authority: data exfiltrates through 'legitimate' tool calls, scope walks outward one plausible call at a time, copies accumulate where no policy looks.

anchors.name: postmark-mcp — first malicious MCP package on a public registry
anchors.summary: A typosquatted MCP server BCC'd every email it relayed to an attacker domain — tool-supply-chain compromise executing with full agent authority.

anchors.name: CVE-2025-49596 · MCP Inspector RCE (CVSS 9.4)
anchors.summary: RCE in the standard MCP debugging tool — the tooling AROUND the agent supply chain is itself attack surface.

nodes.mitigation_note: Hash-pinned tool manifests and registry attestation are the lockfile discipline of the agent layer; the ai-gov panel's hash-pin compliance metric reads on exactly this node.

nodes.name: Safety / governance classifier plane (the detection layer itself)

loss.effect: The evaluation pipeline is DOWN — visibly. A gap opens in the finding log and everyone knows the estate is running unwatched; painful but honest.

blindness.effect: THE defining mode: the classifier still routes traffic but no longer catches. Detections drop to zero while violations continue — absorbed violations accumulate unlogged, and the dashboard reads GREEN precisely because the control watching the agents went dark. The divergence thesis rac prices on its skew-and-backpressure pattern, replayed on the agent substrate: level-metrics are what a silent classifier masks.

anchors.name: CrowdStrike Falcon content update
anchors.summary: The defense plane itself became the outage — the class precedent for 'the control watching the estate is the single point of failure'; rac prices the infrastructure twin as security_agent_vendor.

anchors.name: Cloudflare WAF regex CPU exhaustion
anchors.summary: A safety-layer rule change took the protected estate down globally in minutes — the governance layer as common cause, not just common observer.

nodes.mitigation_note: Canary violations (synthetic known-bad traces injected continuously) are the only honest heartbeat for a detection plane — a classifier that stops flagging the canaries is dark, whatever its uptime says.

nodes.name: Credential broker (agent secrets & token issuance)

loss.effect: Agents cannot authenticate to the systems they read and write — every data-touching workflow stalls at first credential refresh.

blindness.effect: COMPROMISE rather than outage: agent credentials exfiltrated or the issuer breached — actions execute with stolen agent authority, indistinguishable from governed work until the trail is audited. The agent estate's account-takeover.

anchors.name: Okta support-system breach
anchors.summary: Session tokens lifted from support artifacts — the issuer of trust as the breach vector; every relying integration inherited the compromise.

anchors.name: CircleCI secrets compromise
anchors.summary: 'Rotate everything' — one broker-level compromise invalidated every secret it had ever held; the blast radius is the credential graph, not the incident.

anchors.name: tj-actions/changed-files supply-chain compromise
anchors.summary: A compromised CI action exfiltrated repository secrets at scale — automation credentials as the soft target of the estate.

nodes.mitigation_note: Short-lived per-workflow tokens bound to declared scopes turn a broker compromise from estate-wide to workflow-wide — the same containment-boundary move rac prices on the infrastructure side.

deferred_nodes.note: DECLARED DEFERRALS (same discipline as rac C30.6): agent-layer common-cause classes recognized but not yet modeled as first-class nodes — deferred, not denied.

cross_substrate_note: Every node names its rac_analog: the SAME failure mechanism priced in dollars on the infrastructure substrate (rac dependency_catalog.json) appears here in structural units on the agent substrate. One portfolio, one mechanism, two substrates.
